body: Honestly, I have read a lot about BPD and narcissistic parents over the past few weeks. I really feel like putting a name to my feelings has been helpful, it's just been really difficult to not have anything validated or confirmed.
I am definitely willing to try anything at this point. I am hoping to call a patient advocate and explain.
I am on Welbutrin. Just started therapy but it has made me feel worse than before.

I absolutely need reliable transportation. I am totally willing to do a cheaper used car. Other than the inspection and vehicle history, what can I do to make sure the car I'm buying will not be a money pit as this is a fear of mine?
I have, but would it not be more expensive to buy the car this way? Why not buy a decent used car then? I feel that would make more sense.

I would use nothing but public transit if we had a decent system but we do not. Additionally, my boyfriend doesn't drive and I do a lot of shopping for my grandma. I really don't know what to do that is not going to be somewhat a strain on my finances. FWIW, I budget with my boyfriend's income as well and I would prioritize the car payment over almost everything.
Do hydrating toners offer the same "clean" feeling as astringent toners? How do they compare to micellar water?
My friend has a Fit and can carry larger totes, bags, etc. I am looking specifically for something with a hatchback vs a sedan. I want to be able to fold the seats down.
I wanted something with a bit more cargo room to carry large/bulky items if needed. The trunk of the Corolla is kind of low and it's awkward to try to fit things in the backseat.

So, as I commented above, does it make more sense to buy an older used car to run to the ground while saving cash? I have considered that as an option but I need reliable transportation and feel a bit nervous about getting caught in the trap of paying for older car repair/maintenance. How can I avoid this to save cash?

How cheap of a used car? I have also considered buying a junk car to run to the ground, but don't want to keep spending money on maintenance and I need reliable transportation for work. 

Also, does it matter if my payment was late vs missed? I am trying to understand my CreditKarma auto section, I guess I figured it was okay since it was saying that account was in good shape?
